For those who are unfamiliar with what Shintoism is, I'll lay out our primary beliefs:

We believe in a type of deity called Kami, which are often translated as gods or spirits. Neither of these words is a good translation.

Our principal Kami is Amaterasu, she represents the sun and all life. There are many Kami other than her, such as Tsukuyomi, Susanoo, Inari, Hachiman etc.

Shintoism evolved from traditional Japanese beliefs, Japanese Taoism, Buddhism and Confucianism, the latter three being brought over in the 600s CE from China.

Our principal texts are the Kojiki and Nihon-gi. There's also the apocryphal Kujiki (a suspected forgery, but important to read nonetheless)

Our priests are called kannushi (male) and miko (female)

Our places of worship are jinjya (shrines)

Afterlife is a topic of debate with the Shinto Honcho having no official position on the subject

I've been a Shintoist for around 2-3 years now, formerly Buddhist, before that I was atheist and was born an unbaptized Catholic. I reject monotheism, but I believe other types and classes of gods possibly exist, namely paganist traditions, Hindu gods and other polytheistic/polydeistic faiths.

I do speak Japanese, not perfectly, but I can get by with Japanese conversation and prayer.
